methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College partners with Google for free AI training - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Google's partnership with Roanoke College to provide free AI training represents platform-enabled distribution of AI capability beyond metro hubs, though success depends on whether training produces deep fluency or shallow tool adoption.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: A Norfolk native delivering free AI workshops signals grassroots, community-driven capability building in a non-metro hub, suggesting peer-to-peer distribution patterns that could counter concentration if sustained beyond individual initiative.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional resources and formal AI education infrastructure in the state capital, deepening Richmond's metro capabilities while the model's replicability to rural regions remains unclear.

signals.title: Virginia Tech sets course for human-centered AI leadership - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's strategic positioning for 'human-centered AI leadership' concentrates advanced research capability in a flagship university, creating a knowledge hub that could either radiate outward or reinforce the Blacksburg-NoVA-Richmond triangle.

signals.title: Camp Welcomes Hampton Roads Youth to Learn About Cybersecurity and AI - Old Dominion University
signals.signal_reading: Youth-focused cybersecurity and AI camps at Old Dominion University signal early-stage capability building in Hampton Roads' defense-tech ecosystem, distributing foundational AI literacy beyond NoVA but requiring pathways to deep expertise retention.
